source: Household API (uk-budget-household-test on Modal) answers of 27 October 2026 for the example households, with every measure then published selected, and the matching public/data/policy_parameters.json entries. For src/utils/policyBreakdown.test.js.

fuel_duty_rise_deferral.description: Candidate measure. Fuel duty stays at 52.95p a litre through 2027-28 (to 31 March 2028): the rise due on 1 January 2027 does not happen, so the 5p cut continues, and there is no March 2027 step and no April 2027 RPI rise. RPI uprating resumes in April 2028 from 52.95p, so the 5p and that year's RPI are never made up. Rates are day-weighted to fiscal years. Includes the VAT on the lower pump price.

rows.label: Fuel duty, averaged over the year

state_pension_income_tax_protection.description: Candidate measure. From 6 April 2027, people over State Pension age whose total income (the State Pension, with any increments or additional State Pension, plus all other income, savings interest included) is at or below the full new State Pension (rounded up to the pound: £13,037 in 2027-28, rising with it) get an income tax allowance of that amount, so pay no income tax. Above it there is no allowance: £1 of income over the threshold takes the whole allowance away.

rows.label: Income tax allowance over State Pension age

warm_home_discount_top_up.description: Candidate measure. The Warm Home Discount rises from £150 to £250 for winter 2026-27 only: £100 more to each household in Great Britain receiving Universal Credit, Pension Credit, Housing Benefit or income-related ESA. Receipt follows DESNZ's rates: 85% of Pension Credit households and 70% of other eligible households. Eligibility follows England and Wales's 2026-27 core group, so households in Scotland are approximate.

domestic_electricity_zero_vat.description: Candidate measure. VAT on domestic electricity is 0% instead of 5% from 1 October 2026 to 31 March 2028: the zero rate to March 2027, not in the model's baseline, scored with a candidate one-year extension. Applied to electricity spending only, in Great Britain (Northern Ireland keeps the 5%). 2026-27 carries the October to March share of a year's electricity use (about 57%), not a share of its days.

rows.label: VAT on domestic electricity in Great Britain
VAT on domestic electricity in Great Britain, averaged over the year

threshold_freeze_2031_32.description: Candidate measure. The income tax personal allowance stays at £12,570 and the basic rate band at £37,700 (a higher rate threshold of £50,270) for one more year, 2031-32, instead of rising with inflation to £12,830 and £38,500. From 2031-32 policyengine-uk sets the National Insurance primary threshold and upper earnings limit at the personal allowance and higher rate threshold, so they stay at £12,570 and £50,270 too; the employer secondary threshold is not held.

plan_2_threshold_unfreeze.description: Candidate measure. The Plan 2 student loan repayment threshold rises with RPI from April 2027 (to £30,267 in 2027-28), reversing the freeze at £29,385 to April 2030. Repayments are modelled, replacing those reported in the survey, and the revenue figure is the change in modelled repayments.

lha_unfreeze_2027.description: Candidate measure. From April 2027 Local Housing Allowance rates are no longer frozen at their April 2024 level: each April they are re-set to the 30th percentile of local rents, as policyengine-uk determines them from its projected rents, with the national maximum and the March 2020 minimum. It raises Universal Credit's housing element and Housing Benefit for private renters whose rent is above the frozen rate. Northern Ireland's rates, which follow Great Britain's, are unfrozen too.

rows.label: Local rents the LHA rates are re-set to each April, percentile

employer_nics_secondary_threshold_raise.description: Candidate measure. From 6 April 2027 the threshold above which employers pay Class 1 National Insurance goes back from £5,000 to £9,100 a year (£175 a week), rising with CPI from 2031-32 as current law's does; the 15% rate is unchanged. policyengine-uk holds each employer's total cost of employment fixed, so the saving is passed to employees as higher pay in the same year.

unearned_income_rates_up.description: Candidate measure. From 6 April 2027 the income tax rates on dividends, savings income and property income each rise by 2 percentage points on top of current law, which already includes Budget 2025's rises: dividends to 12.75%, 37.75% and 41.35%, and savings and property income to 24%, 44% and 49% at the basic, higher and additional rates. Incomes are held fixed, with no behavioural response.
